source_message.text:
Hi Dusko — quick context on J\_DISP\_LED:

The e-paper has no built-in light, so we're adding an external LED behind it as a backlight. I haven't picked the final LED yet (testing a 5V COB strip first, may switch to a 3.3V frontlight module later), so the circuit needs to cover both.

Please populate for this build:
\- BSS138 (low-side switch, GPIO42 PWM controls brightness)
\- 10kΩ gate resistor + 10kΩ gate pull-down (keeps LED off during boot)
\- 5V jumper on Pin 1 — leave the 3V3 jumper footprint empty
\- 4.7µF X5R 0603 cap from Pin 1 to GND (PWM ripple decoupling)
\- Series resistor footprint: leave DNP (LED strip self-limits)
\- No flyback diode — LED is resistive, not inductive

Worst-case current is ~70mA (5W/m strip × 67mm cut), well inside BSS138's 200mA rating.

The 3V3 jumper + DNP series R footprint exist only as fallback for a future bare-LED option — costs nothing to leave them empty now.

Full spec is in <http://pcb-integrated-v2.md|pcb-integrated-v2.md> under the J\_DISP\_LED rows / pinout / Critical Routing.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Dusko,

USB is fully working after the rework (U3 removed, data lines
bridged), boards enumerate and flash fine. Here is how the power and
AXP2101 behave after that, tested on both boards with identical
results:

1\. DCDC1 idles at 3.16V. The register is confirmed 3.3V (0x82 reads
0x12), so the converter regulates 4 percent low.
2\. Any load transient collapses the rail: SPI flash erase (about
150mA step) or WiFi TX burst (300-400mA) drops the 3.3V below
2.5V and hard resets the ESP32. Brown-out detector disabled makes
no difference, it is a true rail collapse. Adding 330uF external
capacitance does not help. The board cannot run standalone on USB.
3\. It works when powered from battery only (VSYS around 3.8V), but
fails on 5V USB input. So it fails exactly when the buck actually
has to regulate, and survives near dropout.
4\. Writing DCDC1 to 3.4V over I2C helps a lot: boot, WiFi serving and
a full 1.9MB OTA write all pass. But the WiFi calibration surge at
reboot still collapses it. Also strange: the 0x82 write was
ignored on several boots (readback stayed 0x12) and then latched
on a later boot. Other register writes verify fine, and the VBUS
input current limit default is 1.5A, so it is not input limiting.
5\. I replaced L3 with a larger 2.2uH inductor with much higher
saturation current. No change at all. The inductor is not the
problem, the original DFE252010F spec was fine anyway.
6\. During further testing, DCDC1 on board 2 degraded progressively
and finally died: its output now measures about 265 ohm to GND
with everything disconnected, so the output stage is leaking.
7\. With an external 3.3V feed the whole board works perfectly for
hours: boot, PSRAM, e-paper, WiFi, web UI, sensors. Everything
downstream is healthy.

My conclusion: the AXP2101 chips themselves are suspect (bad batch,
counterfeit, moisture damage at reflow, or parts with non-standard
factory programming). I asked the factory for the sourcing and lot
codes. One thing worth checking on your side: the local input
decoupling on the DCDC1 VIN pins in the layout, whether there is a
capacitor close to the pin or only the bulk group further away.

Do you see any other explanation that fits all of this? Hi Dusko,

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The three boards are chained: power board → main board → sensor board. The main board is in the middle, so power enters from the power board (J\_PWR\_PWR) and the main board uses it locally AND forwards it to the sensor board (J\_SENSOR\_PWR). Think of it like a power strip — power comes in one cable, and the main board distributes it both to its own components and passes it along to the sensor board via a second cable.
The INA219 sits in-series on the 3.3V rail right after the Schottky diodes — so it measures the total 3.3V current for everything downstream: the ESP32 itself, plus whatever the sensor board draws, all in one reading.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Dusko — quick context on J\_DISP\_LED:

The e-paper has no built-in light, so we're adding an external LED behind it as a backlight. I haven't picked the final LED yet (testing a 5V COB strip first, may switch to a 3.3V frontlight module later), so the circuit needs to cover both.

Please populate for this build:
\- BSS138 (low-side switch, GPIO42 PWM controls brightness)
\- 10kΩ gate resistor + 10kΩ gate pull-down (keeps LED off during boot)
\- 5V jumper on Pin 1 — leave the 3V3 jumper footprint empty
\- 4.7µF X5R 0603 cap from Pin 1 to GND (PWM ripple decoupling)
\- Series resistor footprint: leave DNP (LED strip self-limits)
\- No flyback diode — LED is resistive, not inductive

Worst-case current is ~70mA (5W/m strip × 67mm cut), well inside BSS138's 200mA rating.

The 3V3 jumper + DNP series R footprint exist only as fallback for a future bare-LED option — costs nothing to leave them empty now.

Full spec is in <http://pcb-integrated-v2.md|pcb-integrated-v2.md> under the J\_DISP\_LED rows / pinout / Critical Routing.

value_updates.gate_pull_down: 10kΩ to keep the LED off during boot

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The three boards are chained: power board → main board → sensor board. The main board is in the middle, so power enters from the power board (J\_PWR\_PWR) and the main board uses it locally AND forwards it to the sensor board (J\_SENSOR\_PWR). Think of it like a power strip — power comes in one cable, and the main board distributes it both to its own components and passes it along to the sensor board via a second cable.
The INA219 sits in-series on the 3.3V rail right after the Schottky diodes — so it measures the total 3.3V current for everything downstream: the ESP32 itself, plus whatever the sensor board draws, all in one reading.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Based on my rough math: on a 70×50 board (3500mm²), components take about 1300mm² (~37% coverage) — that's well within normal PCB density and should route cleanly on 4 layers.

I'd prefer to keep the individual JST connectors rather than consolidate to a 2x15+10p. The modular approach is important for the enclosure, each sensor has its own clean cable, and the boards slide into rails. A single big connector with a fan-out ribbon cable would make the wiring inside the enclosure very messy and hard to service.
Since you already have all the components placed in KiCad, could you just resize the board outline to 70×50 and do a rough rearrangement? I'm not skilled in KiCad, it would take me hours to do what would take you minutes since you already have the full project open. I'd really appreciate if you could try the resize on your end.

Noted about the ESP32 on the edge, that's fine.

value_updates.connector_consolidation_policy: Retain the individual JST connectors and separate sensor cables; do not consolidate them into a 2x15+10p connector with a fan-out ribbon cable.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Dusko,

USB is fully working after the rework (U3 removed, data lines
bridged), boards enumerate and flash fine. Here is how the power and
AXP2101 behave after that, tested on both boards with identical
results:

1\. DCDC1 idles at 3.16V. The register is confirmed 3.3V (0x82 reads
0x12), so the converter regulates 4 percent low.
2\. Any load transient collapses the rail: SPI flash erase (about
150mA step) or WiFi TX burst (300-400mA) drops the 3.3V below
2.5V and hard resets the ESP32. Brown-out detector disabled makes
no difference, it is a true rail collapse. Adding 330uF external
capacitance does not help. The board cannot run standalone on USB.
3\. It works when powered from battery only (VSYS around 3.8V), but
fails on 5V USB input. So it fails exactly when the buck actually
has to regulate, and survives near dropout.
4\. Writing DCDC1 to 3.4V over I2C helps a lot: boot, WiFi serving and
a full 1.9MB OTA write all pass. But the WiFi calibration surge at
reboot still collapses it. Also strange: the 0x82 write was
ignored on several boots (readback stayed 0x12) and then latched
on a later boot. Other register writes verify fine, and the VBUS
input current limit default is 1.5A, so it is not input limiting.
5\. I replaced L3 with a larger 2.2uH inductor with much higher
saturation current. No change at all. The inductor is not the
problem, the original DFE252010F spec was fine anyway.
6\. During further testing, DCDC1 on board 2 degraded progressively
and finally died: its output now measures about 265 ohm to GND
with everything disconnected, so the output stage is leaking.
7\. With an external 3.3V feed the whole board works perfectly for
hours: boot, PSRAM, e-paper, WiFi, web UI, sensors. Everything
downstream is healthy.

My conclusion: the AXP2101 chips themselves are suspect (bad batch,
counterfeit, moisture damage at reflow, or parts with non-standard
factory programming). I asked the factory for the sourcing and lot
codes. One thing worth checking on your side: the local input
decoupling on the DCDC1 VIN pins in the layout, whether there is a
capacitor close to the pin or only the bulk group further away.

Do you see any other explanation that fits all of this? Hi Dusko,

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Dusko — quick context on J\_DISP\_LED:

The e-paper has no built-in light, so we're adding an external LED behind it as a backlight. I haven't picked the final LED yet (testing a 5V COB strip first, may switch to a 3.3V frontlight module later), so the circuit needs to cover both.

Please populate for this build:
\- BSS138 (low-side switch, GPIO42 PWM controls brightness)
\- 10kΩ gate resistor + 10kΩ gate pull-down (keeps LED off during boot)
\- 5V jumper on Pin 1 — leave the 3V3 jumper footprint empty
\- 4.7µF X5R 0603 cap from Pin 1 to GND (PWM ripple decoupling)
\- Series resistor footprint: leave DNP (LED strip self-limits)
\- No flyback diode — LED is resistive, not inductive

Worst-case current is ~70mA (5W/m strip × 67mm cut), well inside BSS138's 200mA rating.

The 3V3 jumper + DNP series R footprint exist only as fallback for a future bare-LED option — costs nothing to leave them empty now.

Full spec is in <http://pcb-integrated-v2.md|pcb-integrated-v2.md> under the J\_DISP\_LED rows / pinout / Critical Routing.

source_message.text:
Based on my rough math: on a 70×50 board (3500mm²), components take about 1300mm² (~37% coverage) — that's well within normal PCB density and should route cleanly on 4 layers.

I'd prefer to keep the individual JST connectors rather than consolidate to a 2x15+10p. The modular approach is important for the enclosure, each sensor has its own clean cable, and the boards slide into rails. A single big connector with a fan-out ribbon cable would make the wiring inside the enclosure very messy and hard to service.
Since you already have all the components placed in KiCad, could you just resize the board outline to 70×50 and do a rough rearrangement? I'm not skilled in KiCad, it would take me hours to do what would take you minutes since you already have the full project open. I'd really appreciate if you could try the resize on your end.
